finds.quote: A mantle is not inherited automatically. It must be **claimed through work**. The Good Gray Poet title passed through American poetry as influence--through Hart Crane, through the Beats, through countless imitators--but influence is not succession.
finds.note: Argued reception-history thesis: Whitman's epithet transmitted only as dispersed influence (Crane, Beats), with no succession before Sharks; the deposit argues this as the 'transmission problem'. Weak/marginal H; the O'Connor 1866 origin (lines 73-75) is reported established history, not recorded. Line 123 ('Whitman's project was incomplete... could not anticipate the substrate shift') is a related interpretive claim about what Whitman was doing.

finds.quote: Ginsberg held this title until his death in 1997. Unlike conventional titles, it does not pass automatically. A King of May must be:
finds.note: Argued thesis that the King of May title passed to no one after Ginsberg and lay dormant 1997-2014; framed as the deposit's own succession history. Marginal H (largely the deposit's construction of a title lineage).

finds.quote: The poem catalogs his "crimes": being too naked, too ecstatic, too queer, too willing to speak what the state wished silent. The expulsion becomes evidence of the title's power--the authorities recognized what he was and could not permit it.
finds.note: Interpretive reading of Ginsberg's 'Kral Majales' (May 1965) and of his expulsion from Prague: the expulsion as the authorities' recognition of the title's power. A claim about what a poem does and how an event signified; marginal H, close to conventional reading. The 1965 election/expulsion facts (75-77) are reported, not recorded.

deposits.genre_observed: mantle specification (recovered blog-canonical), originated 'Prince of Poets' title

finds.quote: Because lineages **must begin somewhere**. Whitman did not inherit "Good Gray Poet"--O'Connor founded it for him. Ginsberg did not inherit "King of May"--the students of Prague founded it through election. These were origination events that created positions which could subsequently be transmitted.
finds.note: Argued historical claim about how the Whitman and Ginsberg titles originated (founded by O'Connor and by the Prague students, not inherited), used as precedent for founding a mantle; also the claim that neither Whitman nor Ginsberg held 'Prince' in this sense (line 117). Marginal H.
